page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.s2.xlarge is an x86_64 virtual machine running on the KVM hypervisor within the ecs.s2 instance family. The server features 2 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or GPU hardware accelerators, necessitating attached network block storage for persistent operational needs. Public IPv4 addresses are not included by default.

Hardware flag reporting indicates that advanced instruction sets, such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX-512) and hardware-accelerated cryptographic functions (AES, VAES), are omitted or disabled in this instance topology. Consequently, performance relies on standard x86_64 execution without specialized vector acceleration. Persistent storage performance remains bounded by the latency and throughput characteristics of connected remote block storage volumes.

With its dedicated core assignment, ecs.s2.xlarge provides consistent baseline compute performance free from CPU credit exhaustion models. The 1:4 memory balance renders it suitable for general-purpose server duties, including web application frontends, API microservices, background job workers, and development or staging environments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.s2.xlarge is a general-purpose x86_64 instance built on the KVM hypervisor within the ecs.s2 family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, offering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server includes no local disk storage or GPU acceleration, requiring network-attached storage for persistent OS and data operations. Advanced CPU instruction sets, including AVX vector extensions and AES cryptographic hardware flags, are disabled or omitted in this configuration. With dedicated CPU allocation, the instance delivers steady compute output without credit throttling. The ecs.s2.xlarge instance is suited for general-purpose application workloads, API web services, microservices, and lightweight utility hosting where specialized compute acceleration and direct-attached NVMe storage are not required.
